    EU Therapists & Clinicians — Parental Alienation Practitioner Directory¶

    Schema version: 1.0 Last updated: 2026-05-27 License: CC BY 4.0 (intended for github.com/AntiAlienate/antialienate-knowledge) Region: EU (DE / FR / ES / IT / NL / BE) Scope: EU-member-state psychiatrists, psychologists (clinical / forensic / academic), psychotherapists and clinical social workers who have (a) worked PA cases as treating clinician or court-appointed expert, (b) published on PA in a peer-reviewed venue or recognised professional publication, or © publicly stated a sourced stance (recognition / critique / middle) on PA. Stance is sourced, not inferred.

    Standards: Primary sources only — national register entries where searchable, practice / institutional website, peer-reviewed publications, court records, named press. Where a fact could not be confirmed from a public primary source it is flagged "not publicly confirmed".

    Stance taxonomy: - recognition — treats parental alienation / Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung / aliénation parentale / alienazione genitoriale / ouderverstoting as a real, assessable phenomenon; operates or endorses PA-specific assessment, expert-witness or reunification work; typically PASG-aligned. - critique — argues the PA construct (especially Gardner's SAP) is operationalised against DV / coercive-control survivors (predominantly mothers and children); advocates DV/trauma-informed alternatives and tighter regulation of expert witnesses. - middle — engages both alienating-behaviour and family-violence frames; differential-diagnosis or systemic / multi-family approach; not aligned with PASG and not in the abolitionist critique camp.

    Critical EU regulatory & policy context (must read before using this directory):

    • Germany (DE): Psychotherapists and physicians hold an Approbation (state licence) issued by the Land authority; psychotherapists must additionally be listed by the Kassenärztliche Vereinigung (KV) or the Psychotherapeutenkammer of the respective Land (e.g. https://www.lpk-bw.de/, https://www.ptk-berlin.de/). The 2023 BVerfG order 1 BvR 1076/23 (case-file already in /case-studies/) is the most important German constitutional ruling on the use of "Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung" framing in custody transfers — every German recognition-camp expert below must be read against that ruling.
    • France (FR): Psychiatrists are registered with the Ordre national des médecins (RPPS number, https://www.conseil-national.medecin.fr/annuaire); psychologists hold an ADELI number (now being merged into RPS at https://annuaire.sante.fr); court-appointed experts are listed on the liste des experts judiciaires of the relevant Cour d'appel (e.g. Versailles, Paris). The 2013 Cass. 1re Civ. 12-14.392 (case-file already in /case-studies/) is the leading French civil ruling cautioning against routine "SAP" findings. The 26 December 2019 circular CRIM 2019-19/H2 of the Ministry of Justice on intra-family violence is the doctrinal anchor for the French critique camp.
    • Spain (ES): Psychologists are registered with the Colegio Oficial de Psicólogos (COP) of the corresponding autonomous community (e.g. Asturias, Madrid, Cataluña); psychiatrists with the Organización Médica Colegial (OMC) provincial Colegio de Médicos. The Ministry of Equality / Delegación del Gobierno contra la Violencia de Género published the 2020 Informe del Grupo de Trabajo sobre SAP (https://violenciagenero.igualdad.gob.es/wp-content/uploads/ALIENACIONPARENTAL_cap2_lib7.pdf), which institutionally rejects SAP as a clinical construct. The 2017 STS 519/2017 (case-file already in /case-studies/) is the leading Spanish Supreme Court ruling rejecting reliance on SAP without independent evidence.
    • Italy (IT): Psychologists are on the Ordine degli Psicologi regional register (e.g. Ordine Lazio: https://ordinepsicologilazio.it/; Ordine Lombardia); psychiatrists on the Federazione Nazionale degli Ordini dei Medici (FNOMCeO). The 2022 Cassazione ord. 9691/2022 Massaro and 2025 ord. 4595/2025 (both already in /case-studies/) define the Italian doctrine: PA is not a clinically validated construct binding on judges and may not be used to disregard the child's stated views.
    • Netherlands (NL): Psychologists are registered in the BIG-register (Wet BIG, https://www.bigregister.nl/) as Klinisch psycholoog or Gezondheidszorgpsycholoog; psychotherapists separately under Wet BIG. The leading Dutch Supreme Court decision Hoge Raad 15 February 2005 ECLI:NL:HR:2005:AR8250 (case-file already in /case-studies/) on contact-withholding remains the doctrinal anchor.
    • Belgium (BE): Psychologists are registered with the Commission des psychologues / Psychologencommissie (https://www.compsy.be/); clinical psychologists/orthopédagogues additionally with the relevant communauté health authority under the 2014/2016 reforms. There is no Belgian appellate ruling that has fully endorsed SAP; the dominant clinical doctrine is mixed.

    Cross-references to other antialienate-knowledge directories: - Wilfrid von Boch-Galhau, MD (Germany), Asunción Tejedor Huerta, PhD (Spain) and Sietske Dijkstra, PhD (Netherlands) already have full entries in /influencers/. Practitioner-level operational detail (current practice address, regulatory status, recent activity) is added here; they remain primary entries in the influencer set. - US-based PASG core (William Bernet, Amy Baker, Richard Warshak, Linda Gottlieb) — full entries in /practitioners-us-therapists.md. Verrocchio (IT) and Tejedor (ES) are the principal European co-authors with Baker / Bernet. - Canada — Hubert Van Gijseghem (PhD, Université de Montréal, ret.) is Belgian-born / Quebec-practising; full entry is held in /practitioners-ca-therapists.md (cross-listed at end of FR section for completeness because his French-language publications form much of the francophone recognition literature).

    Germany¶

    1. Dr Wilfrid von Boch-Galhau, MD¶

    • Country / city: DE / Würzburg (Bavaria)
    • Practice / affiliation: Independent psychiatric / psychotherapeutic practice, Oberer Dallenbergweg 15, 97082 Würzburg; co-founder PAS-Arbeitsgemeinschaft; founding member, Parental Alienation Study Group (PASG)
    • Practice URL: http://www.drvboch.de/ (older site; current activity status — see Notes)
    • Regulatory body: Approbation as Facharzt für Psychiatrie, Psychosomatische Medizin und Psychotherapie (Bayerische Landesärztekammer, https://www.blaek.de/); ResearchGate scholarly profile https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Wilfrid-von-Boch-Galhau-2021148597
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Psychiatry / psychosomatic medicine / psychotherapy; long-term mental-health sequelae of parent-child alienation in adult children of high-conflict divorce; PA as psychological child abuse
    • Stance: recognition
    • Stance source: Boch-Galhau (2018) Parental Alienation (Syndrome) – A serious form of psychological child abuse, Mental Health and Family Medicine 13:725-739 — https://www.gavinpublishers.com/article/view/parental-alienation-a-serious-form-of-child-psychological-abuse-a-worldwide-health-problem and PDF mirror https://www.scivisionpub.com/pdfs/parental-alienation-a-serious-form-of-child-psychological-abuse-and-a-worldwide-health-problem-that-affects-children-and-victim-pa-1977.pdf ; Boch-Galhau (2013) Parental Alienation und Parental Alienation Syndrome/Disorder (VWB) https://www.amazon.de/Parental-Alienation-Syndrome-Disorder-Kindesmisshandlung/dp/3861351781 ; co-translator / co-editor of Gardner (2002) into German https://www.amazon.de/elterliche-Entfremdungssyndrom-Parental-Alienation-Syndrome/dp/3861351773 ; co-organiser International PAS Conference Frankfurt-am-Main, October 2002
    • Programs / publications:
    • Boch-Galhau & Kodjoe (2006) chapter in International Handbook of Parental Alienation Syndrome (Charles C Thomas) — psychological consequences of PAS indoctrination for adult children of divorce
    • Boch-Galhau (2013) German-language monograph Parental Alienation und Parental Alienation Syndrome/Disorder (VWB Verlag, ISBN 978-3-86135-178-2) — the standard German-language clinician's reference
    • Boch-Galhau (2018) Parental Alienation – A serious form of psychological child abuse (English peer-reviewed)
    • Founding member, PASG (https://www.pasg.info/)
    • Primary contact: Practice telephone +49 931 359 2133 (Oberer Dallenbergweg 15, 97082 Würzburg) — verify current activity before contacting; ResearchGate messaging via profile above
    • Tier: 1
    • Hook: German-speaking world's most prolific PA clinician-author; the standard German monograph is his. Any Würzburg / Bavarian recognition-camp conversation cites him. (Cross-listed in /influencers/wilfrid-von-boch-galhau.md.)
    • Notes: Older practice site (drvboch.de) is intermittent. Activity status (active / semi-retired) not publicly confirmed from a primary source in 2024-2026. Treat as the historical anchor of the German PA-recognition literature.

    2. Dipl-Psych Ursula Kodjoe¶

    • Country / city: DE / Emmendingen (Baden-Württemberg)
    • Practice / affiliation: Independent practice in mediation, systemic family therapy and PA-related expert consulting, Emmendingen; long-standing freelance consultant (until 2005) to the Bundesministerium der Justiz and the French Ministère de la Justice on international child-custody disputes; PASG-aligned (recurring speaker, Nordic Conference Stockholm 2018; Brussels 2021)
    • Practice URL: LinkedIn (institutional verification) https://de.linkedin.com/in/ursula-kodjoe-b2815340 ; PASG external resources https://www.pasg.info/external-resources
    • Regulatory body: Diplom-Psychologin + Diplom-Sozialpädagogin (German diploma psychologist / social pedagogue); systemic family therapist and mediator; the Diplom-Psychologin title pre-dates the 2020 PsychThG reform and remains validly entitled to private-practice work as a therapist when registered with the Land Psychotherapeutenkammer. Specific Land Approbation / chamber number not publicly displayed.
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: PA / Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung; international child-abduction mediation; expert testimony in German and Cross-border family proceedings; consensus model for early intervention
    • Stance: recognition
    • Stance source: Kodjoe & Koeppel — credited with initiating the German PAS-debate in the late 1990s (German PAS-Arbeitsgemeinschaft; see Boch-Galhau / Kodjoe / Andritzky / Koeppel update https://oudervervreemding.wordpress.com/2011/11/01/27/) ; PASG Stockholm 2018 presentation "Consensus Model in Germany with interdisciplinary cooperation: early intervention as best prevention" — referenced via PASG event archive https://www.pasg.info/ ; Jugendamtwatch (2014) translated interview http://jugendamtwatch.blogspot.com/2014/04/pas-ursula-kodjoe-dipl-psychologin-zu.html ; Vaeternotruf entry https://www.vaeternotruf.de/ursula-kodjoe.htm ; recent NZZ profile Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung: Wie ein Vater um seine Tochter kämpft https://www.nzz.ch/gesellschaft/eltern-kind-entfremdung-wie-ein-vater-um-seine-tochter-kaempft-ld.1776632
    • Programs / publications:
    • Co-author of the 2011 PA / PAS Update with Boch-Galhau, Andritzky and Koeppel
    • Co-author of the 2006 chapter (with Boch-Galhau) in International Handbook of PAS (Charles C Thomas)
    • PASG Brussels 2021 presenter on the German Cochemer Praxis consensus model
    • Recurring expert in German press coverage (NZZ, Spiegel) on Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung
    • Primary contact: LinkedIn DM https://de.linkedin.com/in/ursula-kodjoe-b2815340 ; practice address Emmendingen — specific street address not publicly confirmed on independent register
    • Tier: 1
    • Hook: German-language clinical bridge between recognition camp and inter-ministerial mediation work; the natural German pairing with Boch-Galhau and a key speaker on the consensus model.
    • Notes: PASG board membership claim in the brief is unverified from PASG's public board page; she is a recurring speaker / contributing expert rather than a confirmed board officer — treat as "PASG-aligned senior expert".

    3. Prof Dr Ursula Gresser¶

    • Country / city: DE / Munich (Bavaria)
    • Practice / affiliation: Private practice for medical-scientific expert assessments, Munich (since 2009); previously Internistin / Rheumatologin with own practice 1999-2009; former senior physician, Medizinische Poliklinik und Rheumatologie, LMU München (1984-1996); former medical director, Springer-Verlag Heidelberg (1996-1998); academic supervisor of dissertations at LMU München (https://edoc.ub.uni-muenchen.de/view/gutachter/Gresser=3AUrsula=3A=3A.html)
    • Practice URL: https://www.ursula-gresser.de/ ; publications list https://www.ursula-gresser.de/publikationen.html
    • Regulatory body: Approbation as Fachärztin für Innere Medizin und Rheumatologie (Bayerische Landesärztekammer https://www.blaek.de/); academic title Prof. via LMU München; not a psychiatrist or psychotherapist
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Internal medicine / rheumatology; medical-scientific expert reports (Gutachten); secondary research focus on long-term somatic and psychiatric health consequences for children of contact-rupture (Kontaktabbruch) to a biological parent — i.e. PA framed as a public-health problem rather than a forensic-psychological construct
    • Stance: recognition (public-health framing)
    • Stance source: Gresser (2015) Macht Kontaktabbruch zu den leiblichen Eltern Kinder krank? Eine Literaturanalyse, NZFam 2015, S. 989 ff. — discussion https://www.buerokratischer-kindes-missbrauch.de/home/wissenschaftliche-basis-bkm-drei-mal-schlimmer-als-der-tod/gresser-studie/ ; Archeviva interview http://www.archeviva.com/kooperationen/offener-bereich/gresser-prof-dr-ursula/weltweite-studien-ueber-gesundheitliche-folgen-fuer-kid-eke-pas-kinder/ ; Vaeternotruf summary https://www.vaeternotruf.de/kontaktabbruch.htm
    • Programs / publications:
    • Gresser (2015) Macht Kontaktabbruch zu den leiblichen Eltern Kinder krank? NZFam 989 ff.
    • Practice publications list https://www.ursula-gresser.de/publikationen.html
    • Numerous Gutachten in German family-court proceedings on health consequences of contact-rupture
    • Primary contact: Contact form / address via https://www.ursula-gresser.de/ (Munich)
    • Tier: 2
    • Hook: The German PA-recognition camp's principal public-health-evidence voice — useful precisely because she is not a psychiatrist or psychologist and frames the issue in somatic-morbidity and mortality data. Cite when responding to "PA is not a real diagnosis" lines.
    • Notes: Gresser's work is contested by mainstream German psychiatry (see e.g. the 2023 BVerfG order's caution on PA framing). Use as evidence of somatic risk not as a forensic diagnosis.

    4. Dr phil Walter Andritzky¶

    • Country / city: DE / Düsseldorf (NRW)
    • Practice / affiliation: Independent psychologist / sociologist; long-time author on the psychosocial diagnostics of alienating parents and on the Jugendamt (Youth Welfare Office) role in custody assessment
    • Practice URL: Author archive (Familie & Familienrecht) https://familiefamilienrecht.wordpress.com/tag/walter-andritzky/ ; PDF Verhaltensmuster und Persönlichkeitsstruktur entfremdender Eltern (Psychotherapie in Psychiatrie, Psychotherapeutischer Medizin und Klinischer Psychologie 7/2/2002) https://eltern-kind-entfremdung.eu/wp-content/uploads/Artikel-Jugendamt-PSYCHIATRIEZTSCHR.pdf
    • Regulatory body: Diplom-Psychologe (German diploma psychologist) + sociologist (PhD); regulatory chamber not publicly confirmed (independent author, not currently listed on any KV)
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Personality-structure and behavioural patterns of alienating parents; Jugendamt role; ethnopsychology
    • Stance: recognition
    • Stance source: Andritzky (2002) Verhaltensmuster und Persönlichkeitsstruktur entfremdender Eltern: Psychosoziale Diagnostik und Orientierungskriterien für Interventionen, Psychotherapie 7(2):166-182 (PDF above); Andritzky (2002) Nicht instrumentalisieren, Deutsches Ärzteblatt (warning against professionals being instrumentalised by alienating parents); summary on Wikipedia https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eltern-Kind-Entfremdung
    • Programs / publications:
    • Andritzky (2002) Verhaltensmuster und Persönlichkeitsstruktur entfremdender Eltern (Psychotherapie 7/2:166-182)
    • Andritzky (2002) Nicht instrumentalisieren (Deutsches Ärzteblatt)
    • Co-author 2011 PA/PAS Update with Boch-Galhau / Kodjoe / Koeppel
    • Primary contact: No public practice URL or current address found — outreach via Familie & Familienrecht archive contact or via PAS-AG channels
    • Tier: 3
    • Hook: Cite his 2002 Ärzteblatt warning when documenting how PA-recognition camp itself warned against professional capture — useful for showing the recognition camp is not monolithic.
    • Notes: Current activity / retirement status not publicly confirmed. Treat as historical-literature contributor.

    Excluded — Germany¶

    • Werner Bartens (Süddeutsche Zeitung science editor, MD): verified as a science journalist and qualified physician (https://werner-bartens.de/lebenslauf/) but not a practising psychiatrist / psychotherapist and no specific PA-clinical publication confirmed. Belongs in a journalists / commentators list, not the practitioner directory. Excluded here for category fit.

    France¶

    1. Dr Maurice Berger¶

    • Country / city: FR / Saint-Étienne (Loire) — and Lyon (Centre Médical de l'Argentière, since 2014)
    • Practice / affiliation: Pédopsychiatre; active in psychiatric practice (consultant at a centre éducatif renforcé + Centre Médical de l'Argentière since 2014); former chef de service de psychiatrie de l'enfant CHU de Saint-Étienne (1989-2014); former professeur associé de psychopathologie de l'enfant, Université Lyon II (1992-2003); psychanalyste; creator of the French DIU Expertise judiciaire en psychiatrie de l'enfant et psychologie clinique de l'enfant at Paris-Cité
    • Practice URL: https://www.mauriceberger.net/ ; CV https://www.mauriceberger.net/curriculum-vitae/
    • Regulatory body: Ordre national des médecins — spécialité psychiatrie / pédopsychiatrie (RPPS number searchable at https://annuaire.sante.fr) ; RPPS not publicly displayed on personal site
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed (verify via annuaire.sante.fr)
    • Specialty: Pédopsychiatrie; visites médiatisées (he coined the term); placement of extremely violent children; expert testimony in custody / family-violence cases; critique of SAP / aliénation parentale framings as dangerous in family-violence contexts
    • Stance: critique
    • Stance source: Berger (2017) Le syndrome d'aliénation parentale : un concept dangereux http://mauriceberger.net/wpmaurice/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/Le-syndrome-dalie%CC%81nation-parentale-06-2017.pdf and https://www.mauriceberger.net/le-syndrome-dalienation-parentale-un-concept-dangereux/ ; YouTube Syndrome d'aliénation parentale ou aliénation parentale : des concepts dangereux https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4khrxcg6Xqs ; Berger in Séparation conflictuelle des parents (synthesis https://www.village-justice.com/articles/separation-conflictuelle-des-parents-quel-mode-garde-pour-enfant-synthese-livre,46396.html); Empan (2009) Les violences masculines occultées : le syndrome d'aliénation parentale https://shs.cairn.info/revue-empan-2009-1-page-31 ; CERE / Belgian synthesis https://www.cere-asbl.be/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/9_alie_nation-parentale_sap_ok.pdf ; ENM / Mines ParisTech controverses entry https://controverses.minesparis.psl.eu/public/promo15/promo15_G27/www.controverses-minesparistech-8.fr/_groupe27/glossary/maurice-berger/index.html
    • Programs / publications:
    • 19 books across the career (multilingual); 107 peer-reviewed articles; 332+ international conferences (per CV)
    • Le syndrome d'aliénation parentale : un concept dangereux (2017)
    • Séparation conflictuelle des parents. Quel mode de garde pour l'enfant ?
    • Architect of the visite médiatisée concept used widely in French family-court practice
    • DIU Expertise judiciaire en psychiatrie de l'enfant (Paris-Cité)
    • Primary contact: Contact form via https://www.mauriceberger.net/ ; Centre Médical de l'Argentière (Lyon) institutional address; no direct email / phone on CV
    • Tier: 1
    • Hook: France's most prolific senior pédopsychiatre on the critique side of the SAP / aliénation parentale debate; the natural French counterpart to Joan Meier (US) or Adrienne Barnett (UK).
    • Notes: His critique is anchored in DV-protective and child-violence work, not in the abolitionist tradition — useful for showing the French critique is clinically rather than ideologically motivated.

    2. Dr Paul Bensussan¶

    • Country / city: FR / Versailles (Yvelines)
    • Practice / affiliation: Psychiatre; expert agréé par la Cour de cassation (since 2007); expert près la Cour d'appel de Versailles (since 1996); expert auprès de la Cour Pénale Internationale (CPI / ICC, La Haye, since 2011); private practice Versailles
    • Practice URL: https://www.paulbensussan.fr/ ; bio https://www.paulbensussan.fr/biographie-cv
    • Regulatory body: Ordre national des médecins — spécialité psychiatrie (RPPS searchable at https://annuaire.sante.fr) ; liste nationale des experts agréés par la Cour de cassation https://www.courdecassation.fr/
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Forensic psychiatry; sexual-offender assessment (notably Outreau); criminal responsibility of mentally-ill offenders; expert-witness work in aliénation parentale cases including disputed allegations of CSA in custody disputes
    • Stance: recognition
    • Stance source: Personal practice site frames PA expertise (https://www.paulbensussan.fr/biographie-cv) ; April 2022 complaint by four French child-protection associations to the Conseil de l'Ordre des médecins alleging that his reports invariably conclude SAP and reject children's allegations — Causette https://www.causette.fr/societe/en-france/syndrome-dalienation-parentale-les-expertises-judiciaires-du-psychiatre-paul-bensussan-dans-le-viseur-dassociations and Enfance & Jeunesse Infos https://www.enfancejeunesseinfos.fr/quatre-associations-deposent-un-recours-contre-lexpert-psychiatre-paul-bensussan-partisan-du-syndrome-dalienation-parentale/ ; Wikipédia https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Bensussan ; YouTube TV28 Expertise de l'aliénation parentale https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dyOeGLmkLWc
    • Programs / publications:
    • La Dictature de l'émotion (co-author, public-debate book on victimology and false allegations)
    • Numerous expert reports cited in French press in CSA / custody-overlap cases
    • Active candidate (publicly stated) to have SAP / parental alienation disorder recognised in DSM-5 — unsuccessful
    • Primary contact: Contact via https://www.paulbensussan.fr/ ; practice in Versailles — specific street address / phone not publicly displayed
    • Tier: 1
    • Hook: France's most visible PA-recognition expert witness, and the centre of an ongoing professional-conduct complaint — a flashpoint figure for any French PA debate.
    • Notes: Active disciplinary complaint at the Conseil de l'Ordre (2022→) is the principal current news item. Use cautiously for outreach; high reputational sensitivity.

    • Practice URL: http://www.roland-broca.com/ ; Aliénation parentale section http://www.roland-broca.com/alienation-parentale ; bio http://www.roland-broca.com/a-propos
    • Regulatory body: Ordre national des médecins — spécialité psychiatrie (RPPS searchable at https://annuaire.sante.fr)

    Netherlands¶

    1. Dr Justine van Lawick¶

    • Country / city: NL / Haarlem (Noord-Holland)
    • Practice / affiliation: Clinical psychologist, family therapist, director of training at LORENTZHUIS (Centrum voor systeemtherapie, opleiding en consultatie, Haarlem) — co-founded 1984 (https://www.lorentzhuis.nl/); Associate, The Taos Institute https://www.taosinstitute.net/about-us/people/institute-associates/europe/netherlands/m-j-van-lawick ; co-developer of Kinderen uit de Knel / No Kids in the Middle
    • Practice URL: Lorentzhuis https://www.lorentzhuis.nl/ ; Taos Institute https://www.taosinstitute.net/about-us/people/institute-associates/europe/netherlands/m-j-van-lawick ; Routledge book page https://www.routledge.com/Group-Therapy-for-High-Conflict-Divorce-The-No-Kids-in-the-Middle-Intervention-Programme/Visser-vanLawick/p/book/9780367109233 ; Karnac author https://www.karnacbooks.com/Author.asp?AID=14768
    • Regulatory body: BIG-register (Wet BIG, https://www.bigregister.nl/) as Klinisch psycholoog / Psychotherapeut; NVRG-erkend systeemtherapeut / opleider (Nederlandse Vereniging voor Relatie- en Gezinstherapie); registration number searchable
    • Registration number: not publicly displayed
    • Specialty: Systemic family therapy; vechtscheiding (high-conflict divorce); multi-family group therapy; demonisation patterns in couples and families
    • Stance: middle
    • Stance source: Van Lawick & Visser (2015) No Kids in the Middle: Dialogical and Creative Work with Parents and Children in the Context of High Conflict Divorces, Australia and New Zealand Journal of Family Therapy — https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273477415_No_Kids_in_the_Middle_Dialogical_and_Creative_Work_with_Parents_and_Children_in_the_Context_of_High_Conflict_Divorces ; Visser et al. (2021) Group Therapy for High-Conflict Divorce: The 'No Kids in the Middle' Intervention Programme (peer-reviewed evaluation) https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348979513_Group_Therapy_for_High-Conflict_Divorce_The_No_Kids_in_the_Middle_Intervention_Programme ; Kinderen uit de Knel book https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286921968_Kinderen_uit_de_Knel_Een_interventie_voor_gezinnen_verwikkeld_in_een_vechtscheiding ; Routledge workbook https://www.amazon.com/Group-Therapy-High-Conflict-Divorce-Erik/dp/0367539616
    • Programs / publications:
    • Kinderen uit de Knel / No Kids in the Middle — flagship Dutch multi-family group intervention for high-conflict divorce; now delivered across the Netherlands and licensed internationally (training teams in several European countries)
    • Visser & van Lawick (Routledge 2019) Group Therapy for High-Conflict Divorce
    • Van Lawick (Karnac and Routledge) — multiple monographs on systemic violence work
    • Co-founder Lorentzhuis (1984)
    • Primary contact: Lorentzhuis https://www.lorentzhuis.nl/ (institutional address Haarlem); Taos Institute profile page contact above
    • Tier: 1
    • Hook: The single most operationally significant Dutch contribution to the PA / high-conflict-divorce field — No Kids in the Middle is the Netherlands' export to Routledge and to the European intervention canon. Not PASG-aligned; explicitly avoids "alienator/alienated" labelling.
    • Notes: Treat as the recommended bridge clinician — engages PA dynamics inside a multi-family-group, non-blame frame and has been adopted by Dutch youth-care services (De Viersprong evaluation https://deviersprong.nl/over-de-viersprong/over-de-viersprong-onderzoek/vechtscheidingsbehandeling-kinderen-uit-de-knel).

    • Stance: middle (coercive-control bridge)
    • Stance source: Dijkstra (2022) "I see a wall and then I cannot reach my son": Coercive control tactics by one parent alienate the child from the other, Journal of Gender-Based Violence ; Hoe herken en doorzie je een instrumenteel geweldspatroon? De noodzaak om coercive control te erkennen (2020) https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342355672 ; Sozio (2020) special issue on huiselijk geweld with Dijkstra contribution https://www.sozio.nl/literatuurlijst---sozio-special-hg-2020---ouderverstoting-sietske-dijkstra/1029446 ; RINO-Groep interview Meer zicht op geweldspatronen verbetert de hulp bij complexe scheidingen https://www.rinogroep.nl/interview/331/meer-zicht-op-geweldspatronen-verbetert-de-hulp-bij-complexe-scheidingen.html

    • Hook: The European coercive-control bridge clinician; what serious PA-recognition advocates have to answer to be credible on family-violence intersections. (Cross-listed in /influencers/sietske-dijkstra.md.)

    Honest gaps: - Germany: No critique-camp practising German clinician verified at directory standard in this batch — the German critique tradition runs predominantly through legal academics (e.g. von Hippel) and feminist NGOs rather than named clinicians; a follow-up pass on the DGPPN / DGfPI is needed. - France: Berger is the sole verified critique-camp clinician at Tier 1; a follow-up pass on FENAMEF / Fondation pour l'Enfance evaluators would help. - Italy: Zero critique-camp clinicians at directory standard — the Italian critique runs through the Cassazione case-law itself (Massaro 2022; ord. 4595/2025 — both in /case-studies/) and through legal scholarship, not through named treating clinicians who have published on the topic. This is a structural finding, not a research gap. - Belgium: Only one entry verified to directory standard. The Belgian field is structurally small; the working population on this topic is mostly francophone mediation / academic — a follow-up pass on Femmes de Droit, Yapaka (https://www.yapaka.be/sites/yapaka.be/files/actualite/_alie_nation_parentale_rapport_final.pdf) and the Code analysis (https://lacode.be/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Analyse_Lalienation-parentale-un-concept-a-risques-pour-les-enfants-et-leurs-droits_Oct2023.pdf) would help. - Netherlands: No critique-camp clinician at directory standard — the closest is Dijkstra in the middle-camp; the Dutch critique runs through Schadefonds compensation case-law and the Knel-evaluation rather than through named clinicians explicitly opposing the PA frame.

    Excluded practitioners with regulatory disclosure: - Werner Bartens (DE) — qualified MD, Süddeutsche Zeitung science editor; not a practising psychiatrist / psychotherapist; belongs in journalists list. - Antonella Boschi (IT) — no Italian Ordine entry or PA publication found under that exact spelling; not publicly verifiable. - Liesbet Nieuwenhuys (BE) — no Belgian Commission des psychologues entry or PA-relevant professional profile found under that exact spelling; not publicly verifiable. - Marc Lormans (BE) — no Belgian register entry, publication or named press coverage found; not publicly verifiable.

    All four are excluded pending a more specific identifier (Ordine / chamber number, named publication, institutional affiliation). If the brief intended different individuals than the search returned, please supply additional context.
